title: Vibes won't cut it — Chris Kelly, Augment Code
talk_summary: Chris Kelly argues that AI-generated code is still production code, so the real work is changing software safely, not maximizing generated volume. He recommends giving agents the same scaffolding as human engineers: documented standards, reproducible environments, fast tests, clear task boundaries, and strong code review.

takeaways.technique: Review by change intent, not file order
takeaways.what_they_do: Criticizes current review tools that present lexicographically sorted changed files, arguing review should reflect how the software change is structured and reasoned about.
takeaways.evidence_quote: That's not a way to think about how software changes is in the order of the files.

takeaways.what_they_do: Starts every project with a rules file describing stack and guidelines, and always includes it in LLM context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I always start all of my projects with like here's the stack I'm using. Here's the like guidelines I want you to use.

takeaways.technique: Create-refine loop with a plan markdown file
takeaways.what_they_do: Have the LLM generate a markdown plan, save it, feed it back as context for implementation, then refine with edits in a loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Write a markdown file that would like lay out the plan. Here's my plan. Save that as a markdown file. Then use that again in your context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Warns against vague instructions like 'extract this module using the strangler pattern' and requires clearly defined tasks and boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're never going to give AI the idea of like uh extract this module using the strangler pattern. What does that even mean to an AI

takeaways.technique: Reproducible envs and fast local tests as agent prerequisites
takeaways.what_they_do: Lists documented standards, reproducible dev environments, easy fast testing, clear boundaries, and defined tasks as what makes codebases AI-writable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have reproducible environments... We want to have easy testing... can you run your tests locally? Can is that fast?

takeaways.technique: Treat code review as the core engineering skill
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues code review is the most important skill as agents write more code, and that review tooling today is inadequate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: code review is by far the most important skill... our code review tools today frankly suck
